meta.title: Self-Healing Code Agent — 19-Fix Upgrade Implementation
meta.description: A structured implementation plan to transform the Self-Healing Code Agent from a well-engineered LLM pipeline into a genuine agentic AI system. This prompt contains 19 fixes organized into 4 phases. Each fix includes the problem description, the exact files to modify or create, reference code, and tests to add. Implement each fix sequentially within its phase, and run tests after each fix to verify nothing is broken.

project_context.current_structure: agent/ — LangGraph state machine and node implementations __init__.py events.py — Event dataclass and event constructors graph.py — Graph topology: build_graph(), run_agent(), stream_agent() state.py — AgentState TypedDict, IterationRecord nodes/ __init__.py generate_solution.py — Generator node (initial + repair) create_adversarial_tests.py — QA adversarial node execute_solution.py — Sandbox execution node diagnose_failure.py — Debugger diagnosis node update_learning_log.py — Memory summarizer node framework/ — Async event bus and streaming event_bus.py streaming.py llm/ — LLM router, providers, prompt loading base.py — BaseLLMProvider, InferenceRequest, InferenceResponse context_builder.py — Token-aware context builder (HAS A BUG — Fix 1) prompt_loader.py — YAML prompt loader router.py — LLMRouter: prompt → infer → validate pipeline schema_validator.py — JSON parse + jsonschema validation + coercion providers/ ollama_provider.py hf_provider.py mock_provider.py sandbox/ python_executor.py — Subprocess-based code execution sandbox prompts/ — YAML prompt templates per agent role generator.yaml qa_adversarial.yaml debugger.yaml memory_summarizer.yaml evaluation/ benchmark_tasks.py — 8 BenchmarkTask definitions metrics.py — TaskResult, compute_summary, save_results run_benchmark.py — Benchmark runner results.json — Precomputed results demo/ app.py — Gradio UI demo_runner.py tests/ test_event_bus.py test_graph_mock.py test_prompt_loader.py test_sandbox.py test_schema_validator.py .github/workflows/ sync_to_hf.yml — Only CI: pushes to HuggingFace (no tests) app.py — Entry point requirements.txt project_map.md
project_context.current_graph_topology: generate_solution → create_adversarial_tests → execute_solution → (pass) END → (fail, iterations remaining) diagnose_failure → update_learning_log → increment_iteration → generate_solution → (fail, max iterations) END

global_rules.rule: Implement fixes in the order listed within each phase.
Run `LLM_PROVIDER=mock pytest -v` after each fix to confirm nothing is broken.
Maintain backward compatibility — existing mock tests must continue passing.
All new code must include docstrings explaining the design decision.
All new features must be optional and configurable — never break the default "development" flow.
Use type hints throughout. Use `dict[str, Any]` style (Python 3.11+), not `Dict[str, Any]`.
Add each new dependency to requirements.txt.
Never hardcode API keys or secrets. Use environment variables.

When creating new files, follow the existing code style: docstrings at module level explaining design decisions, logging via `logging.getLogger(__name__)`, async functions for all node implementations.

cross_cutting_concerns.concern:
Multiple fixes add new nodes that emit events. For each new node, you MUST also update:
1. agent/events.py — Add new event type constants and constructor helpers: - SPEC_TESTS_GENERATED = "spec_tests_generated" (Fix 5) - CRITIC_REVIEW = "critic_review" (Fix 15) - REPAIR_REVIEW = "repair_review" (Fix 12) - PARALLEL_REPAIR = "parallel_repair" (Fix 14) - TOOL_USE = "tool_use" (Fix 6) Add corresponding constructor helpers following the existing pattern (e.g. spec_tests_event(), critic_event()).
2. framework/streaming.py — Add new event types to the PUBLIC_EVENT_TYPES set. Add format_event_for_timeline() handlers for each new type. Import the new constants from agent.events.
3. demo/demo_runner.py — Update DemoUIState.apply_event() to handle new event types (display critic verdict, show tool use actions, indicate HITL pause).
Apply these updates alongside the fix that introduces each new node, not as a separate step.

The Ollama provider returns real token counts. The HuggingFace provider returns -1 for both input_tokens and output_tokens. The Mock provider returns word-count approximations. All metrics code must handle -1 gracefully — treat as "unknown" in aggregations, not zero.

fix.title: Fix the Context Builder Bug
fix.problem: In llm/context_builder.py, the build_context() function computes trimmed_vars by truncating large variable fields, but then returns the ORIGINAL rendered_template unchanged. The trimmed_vars dict is never used to re-render. The truncation logic is dead code.

file.what_to_change: 1. Add a new parameter `template_str: str = ""` to build_context() — this receives the raw template string before variable substitution. 2. After computing trimmed_vars, RE-RENDER using the template_str with the truncated variables instead of returning the original rendered_template. 3. Add a fallback for when template_str is not provided: do string replacement of the original variable values with the truncated values in the rendered_template.

Add a get_raw_template(role, template_key) function that returns the raw template string BEFORE variable substitution. The router needs this for build_context(). Implementation: load the YAML, access templates[template_key], return it directly.
file.reference_code: def get_raw_template(role: str, template_key: str) -> str: """Return the raw template string before variable substitution.""" data = _load_yaml(role) templates = data.get("templates", {}) if template_key not in templates: available = list(templates.keys()) raise KeyError(f"Template '{template_key}' not found for role '{role}'. Available: {available}") return templates[template_key]

file.what_to_change: Update the call() method to: 1. Import and call get_raw_template() alongside render_template() 2. Pass the raw template string as template_str to build_context()

file.reference_code:
"""Tests for context builder — verifies truncation actually applies.""" import pytest from llm.context_builder import build_context
def test_truncation_actually_applies(): huge_var = "x" * 50000 template = "Code: {code}" rendered = template.format(code=huge_var) result = build_context(rendered, {"code": huge_var}, template_str=template, max_context_tokens=100) assert len(result) < len(rendered) assert "TRUNCATED" in result
def test_no_truncation_when_within_budget(): small_var = "def f(): pass" template = "Code: {code}" rendered = template.format(code=small_var) result = build_context(rendered, {"code": small_var}, template_str=template, max_context_tokens=5000) assert result == rendered
def test_truncation_without_template_str_fallback(): huge_var = "x" * 50000 rendered = f"Code: {huge_var}" result = build_context(rendered, {"code": huge_var}, max_context_tokens=100) assert len(result) < len(rendered)

fix.title: Add Held-Out Reference Tests to the Benchmark
fix.problem: The benchmark reports "80% repair effectiveness" but only checks whether the agent's OWN generated tests pass. The reference_tests field exists in BenchmarkTask but is never populated or used. The metric is circular and meaningless.

file.what_to_change: 1. Add a new field `reference_test_code: str = ""` to the BenchmarkTask dataclass. 2. Populate reference_test_code for ALL 8 existing tasks with comprehensive ground-truth assert statements. Each task should have 5-10 reference tests covering edge cases the QA agent might miss. 3. Reference tests must be executable Python assert statements that test the function defined by the task description.
file.guidance: Write thorough reference tests for each of the 8 tasks: - interval_merge_001: empty, single, touching, overlapping, contained, unsorted - csv_normalize_001: missing keys, None values, partial phone strings, whitespace - log_dedup_001: order preservation, whitespace, duplicates, empty input - flatten_nested_001: strings not flattened, None preserved, empty nested, mixed types - word_frequency_001: case insensitive, punctuation, ties, apostrophes, k > unique - range_compression_001: dedup, single element, consecutive, non-consecutive - safe_divide_001: zero, -0.0, inf, -inf, nan, normal division - anagram_groups_001: case insensitive, deterministic ordering, non-alpha chars, empty

file.what_to_change: 1. Add an async function validate_against_reference(task, final_code) that runs the agent's final code against the task's reference_test_code using sandbox.python_executor.execute. 2. Call validate_against_reference in _extract_task_result after the agent completes. 3. Add reference_test_passed: bool field to TaskResult. 4. Update compute_summary to report both self_reported_success and reference_validated_success.
file.reference_code: async def validate_against_reference(task: BenchmarkTask, final_code: str) -> bool | None: """Run the agent's final code against held-out reference tests.""" if not task.reference_test_code: return None from sandbox.python_executor import execute result = await execute( solution_code=final_code, test_code=task.reference_test_code, ) return result.passed

file.what_to_change: Add reference_test_passed: bool | None = None to TaskResult. Update compute_summary to calculate reference_validated_success and repair_effectiveness_validated alongside existing metrics. Update save_results to include both metric sets.

fix.title: Fix the Test Suite
fix.problem: 397 lines of tests, all using the mock provider. They verify plumbing, not behavior. No edge case coverage for schema validation, no error recovery testing, no sandbox security tests. The terminal status assertion accepts "running" as valid, which is wrong.

file.what_to_change: IMPORTANT: The existing file already tests markdown fences, prose prefix, invalid JSON, and nested dict coercion. Do NOT duplicate. Only add genuinely new tests: - test_truncated_json_salvages_code: Truncated JSON where _salvage_code_field kicks in - test_multiple_json_objects_extracts_first: Multiple JSON objects, extract first - test_code_with_escaped_quotes: Code containing escaped quotes Use _SIMPLE_SCHEMA already defined in the file.
file.reference_code:
def test_truncated_json_salvages_code(): """Simulates max_new_tokens cutting off the JSON mid-way.""" raw = '{"code": "def add(a,b):\\n return a+b\\n", "explanation": "adds tw' result = parse_and_validate(raw, _SIMPLE_SCHEMA) assert "def add" in result["code"]
def test_multiple_json_objects_extracts_first(): """When model outputs explanation then JSON then more text.""" raw = 'Let me think... {"code": "x = 1"} That should work. {"code": "x = 2"}' result = parse_and_validate(raw, _SIMPLE_SCHEMA) assert result["code"] == "x = 1"
def test_code_with_escaped_quotes(): """Code containing escaped quotes inside JSON string.""" raw = '{"code": "def f():\\n return \\"hello\\"\\n", "explanation": "returns string"}' result = parse_and_validate(raw, _SIMPLE_SCHEMA) assert '\\"hello\\"' in result["code"] or '"hello"' in result["code"]

file.what_to_change: IMPORTANT: test_timeout_enforcement already exists (tests infinite loop via while True). Do NOT duplicate. Only add genuinely new tests: - test_memory_bomb_handled: allocate ~1GB, should fail - test_import_error_captured: import nonexistent module, should be captured - test_solution_and_test_code_both_empty: edge case with empty inputs

Create a new test file for router retry behavior: - test_router_retries_on_schema_failure: Provider returns garbage twice then valid JSON. Verify router retries and succeeds on third attempt. - test_router_raises_after_max_retries: Provider always returns garbage. Verify StructuredOutputError is raised after 3 attempts.

fix.title: Make the QA Agent Actually Adversarial — Dual-Oracle Testing
fix.problem: The QA agent reads the implementation and generates tests that validate what the code DOES, not what it SHOULD do. The system can converge on a confidently wrong solution that passes its own tests. There is no oracle.

file.what_to_change: Add a new template called "generate_from_spec" that generates tests from the task description ONLY, without seeing any code. This template should instruct the LLM to act as a QA engineer writing tests BEFORE implementation, based solely on the specification. It should generate 8-12 assert statements covering happy path, empty inputs, None, single elements, boundaries, negatives, zero, duplicates, and large inputs.

Add two new fields to AgentState: - spec_test_code: str (generated once from task description, blind to code) - adversarial_test_code: str (generated per iteration, sees the code) Rename the existing current_test_code usages to adversarial_test_code, or keep current_test_code as an alias for backward compatibility.

Create a new node that generates specification-based tests. This node: 1. Calls router.call() with role="qa_adversarial", template_key="generate_from_spec" 2. Only passes task_description as a variable (NO code) 3. Returns {"spec_test_code": result["test_code"]} 4. Only runs at iteration 0 (checked in the graph wiring, not in the node itself)

Update execute_solution to run BOTH test suites: 1. Run spec tests: execute(current_code, spec_test_code) 2. Run adversarial tests: execute(current_code, adversarial_test_code) 3. Both must pass for overall success 4. Failure summary should clearly separate "SPEC TEST FAILURES" from "ADVERSARIAL TEST FAILURES" Handle the case where spec_test_code is empty (when spec tests are disabled).

Add the generate_spec_tests node to the graph. Wire it as the entry point (before generate_solution) when spec tests are enabled. The flow becomes: generate_spec_tests → generate_solution → create_adversarial_tests → execute_solution On repair iterations, skip generate_spec_tests (it only runs once).

fix.title: Add Graceful Degradation and Error Recovery
fix.problem: If schema validation fails 3 times in a row, router.call() raises StructuredOutputError and the entire agent run crashes. No fallback behavior, no partial results.

file.what_to_change: 1. Add a call_with_fallback() method that wraps call() in a try/except. 2. Add a _get_fallback(role, raw_text) method that returns safe defaults per role: - debugger: generic diagnosis with confidence=0.1 - qa_adversarial: fallback smoke test "assert True" - generator: attempt to extract code from markdown fences in raw_text - memory_summarizer: generic "no lessons extracted" message 3. Nodes should use call_with_fallback() for non-critical roles (debugger, memory_summarizer). Generator and QA should still use call() since their failure is truly unrecoverable.
Add `degraded_nodes: list[str]` field to AgentState to track which nodes used fallback behavior.
Switch from router.call() to router.call_with_fallback() so diagnosis failures don't crash the entire run. If fallback is used, append "diagnose_failure" to degraded_nodes.
Add confidence-aware routing after diagnosis. If the debugger's confidence is below 0.3, route to a "blind retry" (regenerate from scratch) instead of targeted repair.

fix.title: Improve the Sandbox
fix.problem: Solution code and test code run in the same namespace. Tests can couple to implementation internals (helper functions, module-level variables, side effects).

file.what_to_change: 1. Write solution code to a SEPARATE temp file. 2. Update the sandbox wrapper to use importlib.util to load the solution as an isolated module, then inject only public names (not starting with _) into the test namespace via globals(). 3. Add resource limits using the resource module via preexec_fn on the subprocess: - RLIMIT_AS: 256MB max memory - RLIMIT_CPU: 10 seconds max CPU time - RLIMIT_NPROC: 0 (no subprocesses) 4. Update the module docstring to document the security layering: Layer 1: subprocess isolation, Layer 2: rlimit resource limits, Layer 3: importlib namespace separation, Layer 4 (production): nsjail/Docker

fix.title: Human-in-the-Loop with LangGraph interrupt()
fix.problem: Using LangGraph but completely ignoring its flagship capability: interrupt(). For enterprise agent systems, human oversight is the entire point.

file.what_to_change: Create AgentConfig dataclass with autonomy_level field: - "full_auto": no interrupts (current behavior, default) - "review_repairs": pause before each repair for human approval - "review_all": pause before generation AND repair Also include max_iterations, and placeholder fields for features from later fixes (parallel_strategies, enable_critic, enable_spec_tests, enable_cross_session_memory, enable_checkpointing, persist_checkpoints, model_overrides). Add classmethod presets: development(), staging(), production().

Create a human-in-the-loop review node using LangGraph's interrupt(). The node presents the diagnosis (root_cause, failure_category, repair_strategy, confidence, code preview) to the human and waits for a decision: - "approve": continue with existing strategy - "edit": update repair_strategy and/or root_cause with human-provided values - "abort": end the agent run via Command(goto="__end__")
Update build_graph() to accept AgentConfig. Conditionally add the review_repair node when autonomy_level is not "full_auto". Wire it between update_learning_log and increment_iteration.

IMPORTANT: The current run_demo_sync() uses asyncio.run() which creates a fresh event loop and blocks until completion. This is INCOMPATIBLE with interrupt() since the graph pauses mid-execution and needs a separate Command(resume=...) call to continue.
When autonomy_level != "full_auto": 1. Switch demo/app.py to use Gradio's native async support (async generator functions). 2. Remove the run_demo_sync wrapper for HITL mode. 3. When the graph yields an __interrupt__ state, yield the interrupt payload to the UI, wait for user input via Gradio components, then resume with graph.invoke(Command(resume=decision), config).
When autonomy_level == "full_auto", the existing sync wrapper can be kept.
Also update run_demo_async() to accept AgentConfig parameter and pass it to build_graph(). Update DemoUIState.apply_event() to handle the new REPAIR_REVIEW event type.

Add interrupt handling UI components (initially hidden): - A review panel with diagnosis display, Approve/Edit/Abort buttons - When interrupt event is received, show the panel - On user action, call graph.invoke(Command(resume=decision), config)
Also update build_app() to accept AgentConfig parameter.

fix.title: Checkpointing and Time-Travel Debugging
fix.problem: If the agent fails at iteration 3 of 4, everything is lost. No way to rewind, inspect, or fork from a previous checkpoint.

file.what_to_change: 1. Import InMemorySaver and SqliteSaver from langgraph.checkpoint. 2. In build_graph(), add checkpointing based on AgentConfig: - If persist_checkpoints: use SqliteSaver with ".agent_checkpoints.db" - Else if enable_checkpointing: use InMemorySaver - Else: no checkpointer (compile without it) 3. Update run_agent() and stream_agent() to accept and pass thread_config with a thread_id for checkpoint tracking. 4. Add run_agent_with_history() that returns both final state and checkpoint history. 5. Add fork_from_iteration() that rewinds to a specific iteration, modifies state, and replays forward.
file.reference_code:
import uuid from langgraph.checkpoint.memory import InMemorySaver
async def run_agent_with_history(task_description, config, router): app = build_graph(config=config, router=router) thread_config = {"configurable": {"thread_id": str(uuid.uuid4())}} initial_state = _make_initial_state(task_description, config.max_iterations) final_state = await app.ainvoke(initial_state, thread_config) history = list(app.get_state_history(thread_config)) return final_state, history
async def fork_from_iteration(app, thread_config, target_iteration, modified_state): history = list(app.get_state_history(thread_config)) target = next((s for s in history if s.values.get("iteration") == target_iteration), None) if not target: raise ValueError(f"No checkpoint found for iteration {target_iteration}") fork_config = app.update_state(target.config, values=modified_state, as_node="diagnose_failure") return await app.ainvoke(None, fork_config)

fix.title: Add Real Tool Use — ReAct Debugger
fix.problem: Every "agent" is just an LLM call with a different prompt. There is no tool use, no autonomous decision-making, no ReAct-style reasoning. This is a pipeline, not an agent.

file.what_to_change:
Create three debugger tools using @tool decorator from langchain_core.tools:
1. run_snippet(code: str) -> str Execute a short Python snippet to test a hypothesis about a bug. Uses sandbox executor with 5s timeout. Returns stdout + stderr.
2. inspect_function(code: str, function_name: str) -> str Parse AST to extract function signature, arguments, and docstring. Returns structured info about the function.
3. diff_iterations(code_v1: str, code_v2: str) -> str Show unified diff between two code versions using difflib. Returns the diff output.

Restructure diagnose_failure to use a ReAct loop with tools. Instead of a single LLM call, the debugger should: 1. Be given the tools (run_snippet, inspect_function, diff_iterations) bound via bind_tools() 2. Operate in a think → act → observe loop using LangGraph's ToolNode pattern 3. The LLM decides whether to use a tool or provide the final diagnosis 4. When it returns the final structured diagnosis (no tool calls), the loop ends
This can be implemented as either: a) A sub-graph with "reason" and "tools" nodes plus conditional routing, OR b) A simple loop within the node function that calls the LLM, checks for tool_calls, executes them, feeds results back, and repeats until done.
Choose approach (b) if the LLM provider doesn't support native tool calling (Ollama with llama3 may not). In that case, instruct the LLM to output a special JSON structure indicating tool use vs final diagnosis.

fix.note: langchain-core is already in requirements.txt (langchain-core>=0.3.0) — no new dependency needed for the @tool decorator. Do NOT add it again.

fix.title: Parallel Repair Strategies with Tournament Selection
fix.problem: The agent tries one repair strategy per iteration serially. If wrong, an entire iteration is wasted.

file.what_to_change: Add `parallel_repairs: Annotated[list, operator.add]` to AgentState. This uses a reducer so parallel branches append their results. Add `strategy_name: str` for tracking which strategy was used.

Create fan_out_repairs() that returns a list of Send() objects, each with a different repair strategy (minimal_fix, restructure, add_guards).
Create parallel_generate() node that generates a repair candidate for one strategy, executes it against both test suites, and returns the result in parallel_repairs.
Create select_best_repair() node that picks the best candidate using tournament selection: both pass > spec pass > fewest total failures.

When config.parallel_strategies is True, replace the single generate_solution repair path with: fan_out_repairs → parallel_generate → select_best_repair. Use LangGraph's conditional edges with Send for fan-out.

fix.title: Agent Self-Reflection / Critic Node
fix.problem: When tests pass, the agent immediately declares success. No sanity check on whether the solution actually matches the specification vs merely passing generated tests.

file.what_to_change: Create a critic prompt with role, system prompt, schema, and review template. Schema: {"verdict": "approve"|"reject", "issues": [...], "confidence": 0.0-1.0} The review template receives task_description, code, and test_summary. It asks the critic to evaluate whether the code actually solves the task, identifies untested edge cases, and checks for algorithmic errors that happen to produce correct output for the tested cases.

Create a critic node that reviews solutions after tests pass. Uses router.call_with_fallback() with role="critic", template_key="review". If verdict is "reject" AND confidence > critic_confidence_threshold (from config): - Set last_execution_passed to False - Set last_failure_summary to critic feedback - Set root_cause and repair_strategy from critic issues - Set status to "running" (re-enter repair loop) If verdict is "approve": return empty dict (don't change state).

When config.enable_critic is True: After execute_solution passes, route to critic_review instead of END. After critic_review: - If approved → END - If rejected (confidence > threshold) → diagnose_failure (re-enter repair loop)

fix.title: Multi-Model Routing
fix.problem: Every agent role uses the same model. The memory summarizer doesn't need the same model power as the code generator.

file.what_to_change: 1. Add role_providers: dict[str, BaseLLMProvider] parameter to LLMRouter.__init__(). 2. Add _get_provider(role) method that checks role_providers first, falls back to default. 3. Update call() and call_with_fallback() to use _get_provider(role) instead of self._provider. 4. Log which model handled each call.
When building the router, check config.model_overrides and create role-specific providers for any overridden roles.

fix.title: Cross-Session Learning with a Vector Store
fix.problem: The learning log resets between tasks. No cross-session memory. The system makes the same mistakes repeatedly.

file.what_to_change: Create LessonStore class using ChromaDB: - __init__(persist_dir): Create/connect to a ChromaDB collection named "lessons" - store_lesson(lesson, task_category, failure_category, task_id): Upsert with metadata - retrieve_relevant_lessons(query, task_category, n_results=5): Semantic search with optional category filter - total_lessons property: Return collection count Use hashlib for generating deterministic document IDs. Wrap all operations in try/except for graceful failure.
At iteration 0, if lesson_store is available, retrieve relevant lessons and prepend them to the learning_log.

When config.enable_cross_session_memory is True, create a LessonStore instance and pass it to the generate_solution and post-success nodes. After a successful run, persist the learning log lessons to the store.
Test LessonStore roundtrip: store a lesson, retrieve it by semantic query, verify it's returned.

fix.problem: The graph topology is hardcoded. Different teams need different configurations. A team building agents for other teams needs declarative configuration.

file.what_to_change: This file was created in Fix 12. Now ensure all 19 fix features are represented as config fields. The final AgentConfig should include: - max_iterations, autonomy_level - parallel_strategies - enable_critic, critic_confidence_threshold - enable_spec_tests - enable_cross_session_memory, memory_persist_dir - enable_langsmith, langsmith_project - enable_checkpointing, persist_checkpoints - model_overrides With classmethod presets: development(), staging(), production().

This is the culmination — build_graph() should now dynamically construct the graph topology based on ALL AgentConfig fields: 1. Always add: generate_solution, create_adversarial_tests, execute_solution, diagnose_failure, update_learning_log, increment_iteration 2. Conditionally add generate_spec_tests (config.enable_spec_tests) 3. Conditionally add critic_review (config.enable_critic) 4. Conditionally add review_repair (config.autonomy_level != "full_auto") 5. Conditionally add parallel_generate + select_best_repair (config.parallel_strategies) 6. Wire edges dynamically based on which nodes are present 7. Add checkpointer based on config Ensure the development() preset produces the same graph as the current hardcoded one for backward compatibility.

Add a preset selector (Radio: Development, Staging, Production, Custom). Selecting a preset configures the agent automatically. "Custom" reveals individual toggles for each config field. Add the selected config to results output for reproducibility. Update build_app() to accept and use AgentConfig.

The root app.py (HuggingFace Spaces entry point) currently creates LLMRouter() without config and calls _prewarm(). After the config system is in place: 1. Read config preset from environment variable: AGENT_PRESET (default: "development") 2. Create AgentConfig from preset via getattr(AgentConfig, preset)() 3. Pass config through to build_app() in demo/app.py 4. If config.model_overrides is set, prewarm each role-specific provider
